commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that a p-value of 0.03 means there is a 3% chance the null hypothesis is true.

fixIt.corrected: The p-value is about the data given the null: if H0 were true, 3% of experiments would give data this extreme. It never assigns a probability to H0 itself.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: state what a p-value of 0.03 actually counts, naming the world in which it is computed.

fixIt.corrected: If the null were true, 3% of experiments would give data this extreme - the 3% counts extreme data under the null, not the chance the null is true.
